channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: AUD/JPY Price Forecast: Holds gains above 114.00, bullish vibe remains intact above 100-day SMA
item.description: The AUD/JPY cross trades in positive territory around 114.25 during the early European trading hours on Friday. The Australian Dollar (AUD) strengthens against the Japanese Yen (JPY) on a strong Australian employment report for June.

item.title: Gold extends slide as inflation fears lift Fed hike bets and USD amid Trump's tariffs
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) attracts sellers for the second straight day on Friday and weakens further below the $4,050 level during the Asian session.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Eyes rising wedge top near 187.00
item.description: EUR/JPY extends its gains for the fourth consecutive day, trading around 186.50 during the Asian hours on Friday. The currency cross is maintaining a bullish near-term bias as price holds above both the nine-period and 50-period Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs).

item.title: United States Dollar Index holds gains near 101.50 on revival of hawkish Fed bets
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) clings to the previous day’s gains in the Asian session on Friday, as surging oil prices due to intensified Middle East energy supply risks have revived Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike expectations.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD holds gains above $57.50 despite rising Fed rate hike odds
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) inches higher after registering over 4% losses in the previous day, trading around $57.60 per troy ounce during the Asian hours on Friday.

item.title: British Pound rebounds above 1.3300 ahead of UK Retail Sales data
item.description: The GBP/USD pair recovers some lost ground to near 1.3325, snapping the five-day losing streak during the Asian trading hours on Friday. However, the potential upside might be limited amid heightened military tensions in the Middle East.

item.title: Canadian Dollar edges higher vs soft USD; bulls seem hesitant amid mixed cues
item.description: The USD/CAD pair attracts fresh sellers during the Asian session on Friday and currently trades around the 1.4070 zone, down 0.10% for the day amid a softer US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Euro rises as US Dollar weakens despite rising Middle East tensions
item.description: EUR/USD gains ground after posting modest losses in the previous day, trading around 1.1380 during the Asian hours on Friday.

item.title: Japan’s Katayama says ready to act appropriately on currency shifts whenever necessary
item.description: Japan’s Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama delivered a verbal intervention on Friday, saying that authorities prepared to take decisive steps on foreign exchange.

item.title: Australian Dollar rebounds vs USD; Trump's tariffs and US-Iran tensions cap gains
item.description: The AUD/USD pair attracts some buyers during the Asian session on Friday and reverses a part of the previous day's slide back to the weekly trough.

item.title: Japanese Yen flatlines near multi-decade low after CPI inflation data
item.description: The USD/JPY pair holds steady near 163.90 during the early Asian session on Friday. However, the Japanese Yen (JPY) remains near a multi-decade low against the US Dollar (USD). The preliminary readings of the US S&P Global Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) will be published later on Friday.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7939 vs. 6.7906 previous
item.description: On Friday, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead at 6.7939 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.7906 and 6.7795 Reuters estimate.

item.title: 10% weekly surge: WTI holds above $90.00 amid Middle East escalation
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price halts its three-day winning streak, trading around $90.20 per barrel during the Asian hours on Friday. However, WTI crude price is on track to surge over 10% this week.

item.title: US President Donald Trump imposes new tariffs on dozens of trade partners
item.description: The United States (US) will impose new tariffs of between 10% and 12.5% on imports from most major trading partners, its biggest move yet to reconstruct US President Donald Trump’s tariff wall that was pierced by the Supreme Court, Bloomberg reported on Thursday.

item.title: US President Donald Trump vows to punish Iran for Houthi attacks in Red Sea
item.description: US President Donald Trump said that the US would hold Iran responsible for the Houthis’ actions and warned that Iran and its Houthi allies would both soon receive a “major military punishment,” Reuters reported on Thursday.

item.title: US military launches 13th consecutive night of strikes on Iranian military targets
item.description: The US Central Command (CENTCOM) said it is attacking Iran for the 13th consecutive night, the Guardian reported on Friday. The US military stated that this action aims to hold Iran accountable and diminish threats from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) to commercial shipping.

item.title: Gold slumps to near $4,050 as Middle East conflict fuels inflation worries
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) faces some selling pressure to around $4,050 during the early Asian session on Friday.

item.title: Japan’s National CPI climbs 1.7% YoY in June, Core CPI rises as expected
item.description: Japan’s National Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose by 1.7% YoY in June, compared to the previous reading of 1.5%, according to the latest data released by the Japan Statistics Bureau on Friday.

item.title: British Pound Sterling slides for a sixth session on a Dollar story Britain had no part in
item.description: Sterling's sixth consecutive losing session arrives without a single domestic headline behind it, and that absence is the more useful fact about Thursday than the 0.45% loss itself.

item.title: Australia's S&P Global Manufacturing PMI rises to 51.7 in July
item.description: The preliminary reading of Australia's S&P Global Manufacturing Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) rose to 51.7 in July versus 51.5 prior, the latest data published by S&P Global showed on Friday.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Upside bias toward 6.7600 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann expect USD/CNH to remain in a narrow consolidation between 6.7680 and 6.7780 intraday after a lacklustre session.

item.title: EUR/JPY extends rally as ECB hike buzz tests Yen risks
item.description: The EUR/JPY extends its advance for the third straight day, set to end the week with solid gains as traders brace for the end of the week.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: BI may still need to tighten – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan reports that Bank Indonesia kept its policy rate at 5.75%, surprising expectations for a hike, as recent Rupiah stabilization allowed policymakers to stay on hold.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar falls as strong US labor data supports the Dollar
item.description: NZD/USD trades lower near the 0.5770 area on Thursday as the US Dollar (USD) strengthens following better-than-expected United States (US) labor-market data.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Holds 218 floor as bulls eye 219 breakout
item.description: The GBP/JPY rotates for the third straight day, as a ‘bullish harami’ chart pattern opens the door for further upside, but intervention fears by Japanese authorities cap the cross-pair advance. The GBP/JPY trades at 218.17, unchanged.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Sideways range holds against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann expect USD/SGD to remain directionless in the near term, with intraday trading confined to a tight 1.2900–1.2925 band. Over the coming weeks, the pair is seen oscillating in a broader 1.2875–1.2955 range as earlier downside momentum has faded.

item.description: Here is what you need to know for Friday, July 24:

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: BI uses incentives over hikes – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay reports Bank Indonesia kept the BI Rate at 5.75%, choosing targeted capital-flow incentives over further tightening to support the Indonesian Rupiah. BI cut hedging costs and improved macroprudential liquidity tools, echoing RBI’s playbook.

item.title: Australian Dollar trades under pressure amid strong US data
item.description: AUD/USD trades lower near the 0.6970 area on Thursday, giving back earlier gains as the US Dollar (USD) strengthens on the back of upbeat United States (US) labor market data and continued hostilities between the US and Iran.

item.title: Asia FX: Oil shock seen manageable – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu argues that Oil near $95 is a shock for Asian energy importers but not a trigger for a broad balance-of-payments crisis.
